title: Concurrent Template Registry
prompt:
Implement `TemplateRegistry` for thread-safe canonical template deduplication. `register(template) -> int` returns a stable zero-based ID. First convert a template string to its canonical form: normalize `\r\n` and `\r` to `\n`; for each line remove leading/trailing ASCII spaces and tabs, then collapse each remaining run of ASCII spaces/tabs to one space; finally remove blank lines only from the beginning and end. Internal blank lines remain. A template whose canonical form is empty is invalid.

Registering an already canonicalized-equivalent template must return its existing ID. A new canonical template receives the next ID in first-unique-registration order. `get(template_id) -> str` returns the canonical template and `snapshot() -> list[str]` returns a copy of canonical templates in ID order. `register` must be safe when multiple threads call it concurrently: one canonical template may appear at most once and every equivalent concurrent registration must observe the same ID.

Use a list for ID-to-template lookup, a hash map for canonical-template-to-ID lookup, and a lock that makes the lookup-or-append transition atomic. Raise `TypeError` for a non-string template or non-integer ID (including `bool`), `ValueError` for an empty canonical template, and `IndexError` for an unknown integer ID.

example.reasoning: The two strings normalize to the same canonical template before the registry checks its hash map.
